newsitem.title: JORDAN: Four-nation group checks Jordanians in Kuwait jail.
newsitem.headline: Four-nation group checks Jordanians in Kuwait jail.

text.p: Representatives from the United States, Britain and the Gulf states of Qatar and Oman will visit Kuwaiti prisons on Monday to check reports that Jordanian inmates were beaten last month, Jordan television said on Sunday.
It said Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti spoke to Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassem and Oman's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Youssef bin Alawi.

"The two ministers told Kabariti that Qatar, Oman the United States and Britain had formed a committee to visit Kuwaiti prisons tomorrow to take a close look at the condition of the prisoners," the television said.

Family members of Jordanian prisoners in Kuwaiti jails say security men beat inmates in Sleibiya prison in Kuwait 10 days ago. One relative, who asked not to be named, said on Thursday three prisoners were still in hospital one week after the alleged beatings.
Kuwait has described the reports as lies "aimed at defaming the state of Kuwait".
Scores of Jordanians and Palestinians were jailed in Kuwait on charges of collaboration with Iraqi forces which occupied the emirate in 1990.
Kuwait's ties with Jordan were strained over Amman's sympathy for Iraq during the seven-month occupation of the oil-rich Gulf Arab state. Jordan has no embassy in Kuwait.
